meta.note: SCOPE DRIFT, not a rename. The write-up framed Purview as data governance only. Microsoft now presents it as three pillars — data security, data governance, data compliance — “in the era of AI”, spanning DLP, insider risk, eDiscovery and compliance management as well as the catalog. The Data Map is still the governance foundation, and the catalog is now named Purview Unified Catalog. Worth deciding later how much of the security and compliance surface belongs in a data-engineering reference at all.

name: Microsoft Purview
oneLiner: Unified data governance, catalog and lineage across your estate.
whatItIs: Microsoft Purview is Azure's (and Microsoft 365's) unified data governance suite. Its data-map component scans data sources — ADLS, Synapse, SQL, Power BI, and even other clouds and on-prem — to build an enterprise catalog of what data exists, where it is, and how it's classified. It automatically detects sensitive data (PII), tracks lineage across pipelines, and provides a searchable catalog with business glossary so people can find and understand data. Purview is the estate-wide 'what do we have and who can use it' layer, broader than a single lake, spanning the whole Microsoft data landscape.

inPractice.narrative: A large enterprise has data in ADLS, several SQL databases, Synapse and Power BI. Purview scans them all into a data map, auto-classifies columns that look like PII, and stitches together lineage showing how a Power BI report traces back through Synapse to raw ADLS files. A data steward curates a business glossary; analysts search the catalog to find the authoritative customer table and see its sensitivity and owner. Purview is the estate-wide catalog and governance record.

coreConcepts.detail: The foundation: a graph of scanned sources, assets and their metadata across the estate, kept fresh by scheduled scans.
Built-in and custom classifiers detect sensitive data types (PII, financial) during scans, tagging assets for governance.
A searchable catalog with business glossary terms links technical assets to business meaning, ownership and definitions.
Captures how data moves and transforms across ADF, Synapse, Power BI and more, enabling impact analysis and trust.
Scans Azure sources plus multi-cloud (S3), on-prem databases and SaaS — its scope is enterprise-wide, not just one lake.
Usage is measured by the data map's capacity units (metadata stored) and the compute for scans/classification.

whenToUse: Enterprise-wide cataloguing and governance across many data sources.
Automated discovery and classification of sensitive data (PII) for compliance.
End-to-end lineage across Azure data services and Power BI.
A searchable catalog + business glossary so users can find/trust data.
Governing hybrid/multi-cloud and on-prem estates, not just one lake.
whenNotToUse: A small single-source project where a full governance suite is overkill.
Fine-grained query-time access enforcement on one lake — that's more Synapse/BigLake-style.
Real-time data processing — Purview describes and governs, it doesn't move data.
Teams entirely outside the Microsoft/Azure ecosystem with narrow needs.

source.quote: Microsoft Purview includes unified data governance solutions for managing data services across your data estate … The solutions include: Microsoft Purview Data Map, Microsoft Purview Unified Catalog.

pricingShape: Purview bills mainly on the data map's capacity units (roughly, how much metadata it keeps online) plus the compute consumed by scanning and classification runs (priced by vCore-hours of scan). So cost grows with the size of your catalog and how frequently/broadly you scan sources — governing a huge, frequently-rescanned estate costs more than a modest one scanned weekly. The underlying data sources are billed separately. The lever is scan scope and frequency versus how much of the estate you truly need continuously mapped.
gotchas: Frequent, broad scans over many/large sources drive scan-compute cost — tune scan scope and schedules.
The data map capacity has a baseline cost that persists as the catalog grows.
It governs and describes data but doesn't enforce query-time row/column access on its own — pair with source-level security.
Lineage coverage depends on connector support; some sources/tools report lineage more completely than others.
Microsoft Purview spans both Azure data governance and M365 compliance — make sure you're looking at the data-governance capabilities you mean.
